stem:
The diagram shows Dev’s model of the Sun and eight planets in order of increasing distance from the Sun, with inner and outer groups marked. A planet is a large, nearly spherical object that revolves around the Sun. He also holds a Moon card.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Inner: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars; outer: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune — and the Moon is not a planet.
The Moon is a planet because it is nearly spherical.
Inner: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune; outer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.
All eight planets are mostly made of gases, so the inner–outer split is only about colour.

teacher.key_rationale: Inner rocky Mercury–Mars and outer Jupiter–Neptune; the Moon revolves around Earth, not the Sun as a planet. Reversing groups or calling all planets gas is wrong.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source force diagram into Sun-and-planets distance strip with inner/outer labels.
